title: tmuxp workspace
description:
JSON Schema for [tmuxp](https://tmuxp.git-pull.com/) workspace files (YAML or JSON).

A workspace file declaratively describes a tmux session: its windows, the panes inside each window, and the shell commands sent to each pane. It mirrors tmux's `session -> window -> pane` hierarchy.

### Required structure

- `session_name` — the tmux session name.
- `windows` — a non-empty list of windows.

### File locations

tmuxp loads a workspace from any of:

- An explicit path: `tmuxp load ./path/to/file.yaml`.
- The user workspace directory (`$TMUXP_CONFIGDIR`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tmuxp`): `tmuxp load <name>`.
- A project-local `.tmuxp.yaml` or `.tmuxp.json`: `tmuxp load .` from the project directory.

### Environment variable expansion

tmuxp expands `${VAR}` style references **before** building the session for these fields:

- `start_directory`
- `before_script`
- `session_name`
- `window_name`
- `shell_command_before`
- `global_options`
- `options` (session and window scope)

Variables inside `shell_command` are *not* expanded by tmuxp — they are evaluated by the shell of the pane (because they are sent via `send-keys`).

Schema version: tmuxp 1.68.x (compatible with 1.10+ for sleep/enter, 1.19+ for window/pane environment variables).

Generated by Claude Opus 4.7 (max)

session_name.description:
Name of the tmux session that will be created (or matched, if it already exists).

This name is what `tmux attach -t <name>` will look for, and is independent of the workspace's filename. Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

**Required.**

windows.description: Ordered list of tmux windows to create inside the session. **Required**, and must contain at least one window.

start_directory.description:
Default working directory for the session. Trickles down to every window and pane unless overridden.

- An **absolute path** (`/var/log`, `~/projects`) sets the directory directly.
- A **relative path** starting with `./` or `../` is resolved relative to the workspace file's directory — this is the idiomatic value for project-local `.tmuxp.yaml` files (`start_directory: ./`).
- `~` is expanded to the user's home directory (remember to quote it in YAML: `start_directory: "~"`).

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

before_script.description:
Path to an executable script run **before** tmuxp builds the session. The exit code is checked: a non-zero exit aborts the build and kills the just-created session.

Typical uses: bootstrapping a virtualenv, installing dependencies (e.g. `pipenv install --dev`), or any precondition that must succeed before the session is usable.

- The script must be executable (`chmod +x`).
- Relative paths are resolved against the workspace file's directory.
- The script runs with its CWD set to `start_directory` (if defined).
- The script's language is irrelevant — bash, python, ruby, etc., are all fine.

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion in the path itself.

shell_command_before.description:
Command(s) sent to **every pane** before its own `shell_command` runs. Trickles down: session-level prepends, then window-level, then pane-level. The accumulated list is prepended to each pane's `shell_command`.

Useful for activating a virtualenv, sourcing a configuration, or changing directory at the start of every pane.

Accepts the same polymorphic shape as `shell_command`: a string, a list of strings, or a list of command objects (with `cmd`/`enter`/`sleep_before`/`sleep_after`).

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion in string values.

global_options.description:
Server-wide tmux options applied with `set-option -g`. These affect the entire tmux server, not just this session.

Common keys: `default-shell`, `default-command`, `default-terminal`, `history-limit`, `mouse`, `prefix`, `status-keys`, `escape-time`.

Values may be strings, integers, or booleans (which tmuxp translates to `on`/`off`). String values support `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

options.description:
Session-level tmux options applied with `set-option`. These affect only this session.

Common keys: `main-pane-height`, `main-pane-width`, `base-index`, `pane-base-index`, `status-position`, `automatic-rename`, `renumber-windows`, `set-titles`.

Values may be strings, integers, or booleans (which tmuxp translates to `on`/`off`). String values support `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

environment.description:
Session-level environment variables, applied via tmux's `set-environment`. Each entry is added to the session's environment so it is inherited by every window and pane.

Note: tmuxp only sets these variables for **future** processes spawned by tmux in this session. They are not directly available to substitutions in the same workspace file — for that, use `${VAR}` referencing your shell's environment when running `tmuxp load`.

suppress_history.description:
Default value of `suppress_history` that trickles down to every window and pane.

When `true` (the default), tmuxp prefixes every `shell_command` with a space so a properly configured shell (`HISTCONTROL=ignorespace` for bash, `setopt HIST_IGNORE_SPACE` for zsh) excludes them from history.

Set to `false` if you want bootstrap commands to appear in shell history.

plugins.description:
List of tmuxp plugin classes to load for this session. Each entry is the **dotted Python import path** of a class that subclasses `tmuxp.plugin.TmuxpPlugin`.

Plugins must already be installed in the Python environment that `tmuxp` runs in (typically via `pip install tmuxp-plugin-<name>`). Plugin hooks include `before_workspace_builder`, `on_window_create`, `after_window_finished`, `before_script`, and `reattach`.

config.description: Deprecated / unused at the workspace level. tmuxp does not consume a `config` key in workspace files. Left here so editors do not flag the field when imported from legacy formats; prefer to remove it.

window.title: Window
window.description:
A single tmux window. A window holds one or more panes.

tmuxp's schema validator considers `window_name` required, but the actual builder accepts windows without one (tmux will auto-name the window from the running command). This schema follows the lenient behaviour: `window_name` is recommended but not required.

window_name.description:
Name of the window (the title displayed in tmux's status bar). Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

Strongly recommended even though tmuxp's builder tolerates its absence: tmuxp's schema validator (`tmuxp.workspace.validation.validate_schema`) treats this field as required.

window_index.description:
Explicit tmux window index. If omitted, tmuxp uses the lowest available index. Useful for keeping a stable mapping between window names and `prefix + <digit>` shortcuts.

Keep in mind tmux's `base-index` option (default `0`) sets the smallest valid value.

panes.description: Ordered list of panes inside the window. Each item may be a shorthand (string or `null`) or a full pane object. See `#/$defs/pane`.

start_directory.description:
Working directory for this window and (by default) each of its panes.

- An **absolute path** or a path starting with `~` takes precedence over the session's `start_directory`.
- A **relative path** (no leading `/` or `~`) is concatenated to the session's `start_directory`. Example: session `start_directory: /var` plus window `start_directory: log` ⇒ `/var/log`.
- `./` and `../` are resolved relative to the workspace file's directory.

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.

shell_command_before.description: Command(s) prepended to every pane in this window, after the session-level `shell_command_before` and before the pane-level one. See the session-level field for shape details.

options.description: Window-level tmux options applied with `set-window-option` **before** panes are created. Common keys: `automatic-rename`, `main-pane-height`, `main-pane-width`, `pane-border-status`, `window-status-format`, `remain-on-exit`, `synchronize-panes`.

options_after.description:
Window-level tmux options applied **after** all panes have been created and their commands sent.

Useful for options that should not be in effect while building — most notably `synchronize-panes: on`, which would otherwise duplicate every keystroke into every pane during construction.

environment.description: Window-level environment variables (requires tmuxp ≥ 1.19). Applied to the window so that new panes inherit them. Overrides session-level entries with the same key.

focus.description: If `true`, this window is selected when the session is attached. At most one window should have `focus: true`; if multiple do, the last one wins.

layout.description: Pane layout for this window. Accepts one of the five preset names (`even-horizontal`, `even-vertical`, `main-horizontal`, `main-vertical`, `tiled`) or a raw tmux layout string captured from `tmux display-message -p '#{window_layout}'` (e.g. `"5e6e,213x49,0,0,1"`).

window_shell.description:
Override the shell or command launched for every pane in this window. Equivalent to `tmux new-window -c <start-directory> <shell>`. Useful combined with `options.remain-on-exit: true` to keep panes visible after a custom command exits.

Panes may further override with their own `shell` field.

suppress_history.description: Window-level override of the session's `suppress_history`. See the session-level field for behaviour details.

pane.title: Pane
pane.description:
A tmux pane. tmuxp accepts several shorthand forms in addition to the full object form:

- `null` (an empty list item: `- ` in YAML) — opens a blank pane that runs no command.
- `"pane"` or `"blank"` — same as `null`, opens a blank pane.
- `""` (empty string) — sends a single carriage return (i.e. opens the pane and presses Enter once).
- any other string — treated as a single shell command to send into the pane.
- an object — the full pane definition (see `#/$defs/paneObject`).

oneOf.description: Blank pane — no shell command is sent. Equivalent to `"pane"` or `"blank"`.

Shorthand pane.

- `""` — sends a carriage return.
- `"pane"` or `"blank"` — blank pane, identical to `null`.
- any other value — single shell command sent to the pane.

paneObject.title: Pane (object form)
paneObject.description: Full object representation of a pane. All fields are optional — an empty object `{}` is a valid blank pane.

shell_command.description:
Command(s) sent to the pane via `tmux send-keys`. Accepts:

- `null` or omitted — blank pane.
- `""` — sends a single carriage return.
- a single string — one command.
- a list of strings — each command is sent on its own line.
- a list mixing strings and command objects (with `cmd`, `enter`, `sleep_before`, `sleep_after`).

Shell variables (`$PWD`, `$HOME`, ...) inside `shell_command` are **not** expanded by tmuxp — they are evaluated by the shell of the pane.

shell_command_before.description: Pane-level commands prepended to `shell_command`, after the session- and window-level `shell_command_before` chains.

start_directory.description: Working directory for this pane. Overrides the window's and session's `start_directory`. Supports the same relative/absolute/`~` semantics as the window-level field, and `${VAR}` expansion.

focus.description: If `true`, this pane is selected after the window is built. At most one pane per window should have `focus: true`.

suppress_history.description: Pane-level override of window/session `suppress_history`. See the session-level field for behaviour details.

enter.description:
If `false`, tmuxp does not append a carriage return after the `shell_command` keystrokes, leaving the command typed but unexecuted. Equivalent to libtmux's `send_keys(enter=False)`.

Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*: behaviour may evolve.

sleep_before.description:
Seconds to sleep **before** sending each command in this pane. Useful before commands that block during shell initialisation (virtualenvs, TUI apps, sourced configs).

**Blocking**: this is a synchronous `time.sleep`, so it delays the entire workspace build.

Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*.

sleep_after.description:
Seconds to sleep **after** sending each command in this pane.

**Blocking**: this is a synchronous `time.sleep`, so it delays the entire workspace build.

Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*.

environment.description: Pane-level environment variables (requires tmuxp ≥ 1.19). Overrides window- and session-level entries with the same key. Applied when the pane is created so that the pane's shell inherits them.

shell.description: Shell (or arbitrary command) to launch this pane with, overriding the window's `window_shell` and tmux's `default-shell`. Useful with `options.remain-on-exit: true` for panes that run a single TUI command (`top`, `htop`, `vim`, a REPL, ...).

oneOf.description: Single command (or `""` for a carriage return).
Ordered list of commands. Each item may be a string, a `null` (blank entry), or a full command object.

command.title: Command (object form)
command.description: Object form of a single command inside a `shell_command` list. Lets you control per-command behaviour (skip Enter, sleep before/after).

cmd.description: The command text sent to the pane via `tmux send-keys`. **Required.**

enter.description:
If `false`, tmuxp does not append a carriage return after the keystrokes for this command, leaving it typed but unexecuted. Inherits the pane-level `enter` if omitted.

Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*.

sleep_before.description:
Seconds to sleep **before** sending this specific command. Inherits the pane-level `sleep_before` if omitted.

**Blocking**. Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*.

sleep_after.description:
Seconds to sleep **after** sending this specific command. Inherits the pane-level `sleep_after` if omitted.

**Blocking**. Available since tmuxp 1.10. *Experimental*.

tmuxOptions.title: tmux options
tmuxOptions.description:
Mapping of tmux option name → value. Used by `global_options`, `options` (session and window scope), and `options_after`.

Values may be:
- a **string** — passed verbatim; supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion.
- an **integer** — used for numeric options (`history-limit`, `main-pane-height`, ...).
- a **boolean** — `true`/`false` are translated to tmux's `on`/`off` (`automatic-rename`, `mouse`, `remain-on-exit`, `synchronize-panes`, ...).

The schema does not enumerate every tmux option — see `man tmux` for the authoritative list.

environment.title: Environment variables
environment.description:
Mapping of environment variable name → value. Used by session-, window-, and pane-level `environment` fields.

Values must be strings (quote integers in YAML, e.g. `SERVER_PORT: "8009"`). Supports `${VAR}` environment variable expansion; values starting with `.` or `./` are resolved relative to the workspace file's directory.

Window- and pane-level environment variables require tmuxp ≥ 1.19.

layout.title: Window layout
layout.description:
Either one of tmux's five built-in layout presets or a raw layout string captured from `tmux display-message -p '#{window_layout}'`.

Presets:
- `even-horizontal` — panes spread evenly left-to-right.
- `even-vertical` — panes spread evenly top-to-bottom.
- `main-horizontal` — one large pane on top, the rest as a horizontal row below.
- `main-vertical` — one large pane on the left, the rest stacked on the right.
- `tiled` — panes split into a roughly equal grid.

A custom layout string looks like `"5e6e,213x49,0,0,1"` (a checksum followed by `width,height,x,y[{...}]`). The schema accepts both forms.
